title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) measuring the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-produced intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model-call accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (20 percentage points). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, clarified provider-call accounting, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility guidance pointing to the archived execution manifest and bundled artifacts.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment demands generated artifacts satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher-order safety/policy constraints. A widely advocated mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, often augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators may miss. Prior surveys and prototype reports document this pattern but provide limited large-scale, preregistered paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution when the same generated candidate is presented to both pipelines. Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a controlled paired study that isolates downstream guarded-stage effects by reusing a single sampled initial candidate for both conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Our preregistered research question is: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete run accounting; (3) a clarified methods description that reconciles provider-call audit fields with the shared_initial_candidate protocol; and (4) an evidence-grounded interpretation and operational boundary conditions for the near-zero guarded benefit we observe.
sections.related_work: Surveys and system papers document the growing integration of LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance in NetOps [1]–[3]. These works emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional—syntactic parsing, command-order/workflow constraints, invariants (for example, keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties may each require different verification primitives. Tool-focused case studies show that static verifiers have expanded rule-sets and topology-aware checks but still leave gaps for runtime-dependent behaviors and stateful sequences; consequently, researchers often layer emulation after static validation to exercise temporal behaviors and state transitions. Empirical prototypes report heterogeneous gains from guarded designs: in some task regimes a verifier alone catches most dangerous errors, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures. This literature motivated our paired design that isolates only downstream guarded-stage effects by enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so that generation variability cannot explain between-condition discordance.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures; deterministic replacement for irrecoverable failures), multiplicity handling for exploratory secondary tests, and contamination controls based on deterministic hashing and artifact-version checks. The planned sample was Npairs = 720 with power planning anchored to a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20.

Task bank and generation semantics. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 task family; the bank covers three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest entry encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, a required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change, minimum_active_in_groups, etc.). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; in the confirmatory run there were no irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses) with client-requested max_output_tokens = 2000; no explicit temperature parameter was set in the client record. Per the preregistration, for each task we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate (one provider call) and that identical candidate was provided to both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or permitted repair invocations) as the only allowable source of between-condition discordance.

Baseline validator and guarded emulation. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements deterministic rule-based checks: vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, workflow atomicity constraints, protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance tests. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then, irrespective of the validator outcome, executes the candidate in an automated sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulation harness records runtime observations (interface admin transitions and transient states, concurrent-interface states, MTU/VLAN application effects, and basic reachability observations) and maps those to runtime-observation rules that can produce a guarded detection when they reveal violations not encoded in the static validator rule set. The emulation-to-detection mapping is intentionally conservative in this study.

Provider-call auditing and reconciliation (clarification). The execution manifest records provider-call auditing fields that summarize model-call events and their classification by stage. Key audited counts from the confirmatory run are: hosted_model_call_event_count = 721, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1, and condition_counts recorded under keys labeled "shared" and "guarded" with values shared = 720 and guarded = 1. These fields enumerate model-call events, not task pairs. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, the single shared initial generation call that produced the candidate for each pair is counted once under the shared_initial_generation stage (hence the audited 'shared' count equals the number of pairs, 720). The guarded pipeline can incur additional model calls only during the repair stage; the single recorded repair call is therefore captured in stage_counts: repair = 1 and in condition_counts under the key that labels repair-associated events. Thus the apparent asymmetry in audited condition_counts reflects event-type counting (one shared-generation event per pair plus a small number of repair calls) rather than an inconsistency in pair accounting. Pair accounting itself remains complete: completed_episode_count = 1440 and complete_pair_count = 720. All provider-call audit fields and reconciliation artifacts referenced here are archived in the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifact for independent verification.

Analysis plan. The primary analysis uses a paired-binary executor with exact McNemar two-sided testing for hypothesis testing and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) for interval estimation. The preregistered primary handling excluded irrecoverable technical pairs (none were present). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory and handled with Bonferroni-adjusted intervals.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential statistics. The paired contingency counts are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model-call accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). No irrecoverable parser or execution failures occurred in the confirmatory set; pair accounting is complete for all 720 pairs.

Discordant-pair attribution. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics any discordant guarded-only detection must arise from either a guarded emulation observation not codified as a validator violation or from a repair-stage invocation tied to the guarded condition. Provider-call audit and stage_counts record exactly one repair-stage model call for the entire confirmatory run; that single repair-stage call corresponds to the unique n10 discordant pair. The archived per-episode traces include the validator_trace and any repair transcripts for the discordant pair; auditors may inspect the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifact to locate the pair identifier and the associated traces.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring traces included validator_trace fields (normalized_configuration, validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count). Those representative artifacts consistently show violation_count = 0 for the vast majority of shared_initial candidates, illustrating that the baseline validator already accepted nearly all generated candidates in this curated task bank. This high baseline success rate explains the near-zero room for guarded-stage improvements under the chosen design and task constraints.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation. The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanations for the negligible guarded-stage aggregate benefit: (1) a validator ceiling effect—deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes the syntactic and workflow checks targeted by the curated tasks, leaving little headroom for emulation to add detections; (2) curated inclusion rules—parser-validated, generator-deterministic tasks reduce exposure to the kinds of noisy or adversarial inputs where emulation typically discovers additional runtime faults; and (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics with minimal repair activity—only one repair call occurred, so the guarded pipeline had almost no additional model-driven opportunities to change outcomes.

Operational implications. For environments that maintain a high-coverage static validator tailored to expected intent patterns and that enforce strong prevalidation, an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may produce negligible incremental detection benefit at scale. This finding is conditional: it does not imply sandboxing is never valuable. In operational regimes characterized by noisy natural-language intents, adversarial misconfigurations, broader vendor-CLI heterogeneity, or long-lived stateful interactions, guarded emulation can reveal runtime semantics and side-effects that static validators cannot anticipate. Practical deployment should therefore consider hybrid strategies: invest in richer static validators for routine, high-throughput changes; apply guarded sandboxing selectively for high-impact changes or high-risk task subsets; and use adversarial/fuzzing task banks to identify validator gaps.

Limitations and scope. The near-zero aggregate effect is specific to our preregistered synthetic task bank, the single validator implementation, the declared/requested model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study’s power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed estimate (~0.0014) is far below that sensitivity and must be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero result for this regime rather than a general negative claim about guarded pipelines in all NetOps settings. Emulation fidelity and vendor-diversity remain important unresolved axes for future work.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream guarded-stage explanations for the discordance. We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated task design. Follow-up work should target adversarial and production-like task banks, expanded vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value.

Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. The canonical execution manifest and the full per-episode artifacts, traces, and analysis outputs are archived together as the reproducibility bundle referenced throughout this paper (consult the execution manifest in the archived bundle for canonical per-file locations and full provenance).
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
